title: Private Estimation of the Overlap-Population Treatment Effect with Rough Covariate Density
banked_reason: The promised complete-class sharp private minimax rate and attaining density-free release are still posed as an open question; the delivered edge bracket and exponent limits are a weaker kernel.
gap_reasons: The promised complete-class sharp private minimax rate and attaining density-free release are still posed as an open question; the delivered edge bracket and exponent limits are a weaker kernel, so the headline contribution must be recast to those proved results or the sharp frontier completed.

The complete constant-factor frontier remains unsettled: for rough smoothness at epsilon=1, the proved MSE bracket runs from n^(-4s) exp[-C_s sqrt(log n)] to n^(-4s), leaving a diverging subpolynomial gap.
The finite private certificate does not determine the optimal privacy-dependent approximation degree or the transition within the rough weak-privacy regime.
Honest length has a separate converse, but its constant-factor relationship to RMSE remains unresolved there.
proof_attempt_summary: Derived a private consecutive-edge benchmark, normalized paired testing priors, finite lower certificates, closed easy regimes and polynomial exponents; the raw growing-degree factorial correction failed covariance and sensitivity checks. The complete rough-design sharp point and interval frontiers still require new estimator and converse mathematics, so an independent validity gate confirmed incremental below-field banking. No Lean formalization was attempted; the repaired published-model inclusion and finite-ECC corollary remain registry-unverified after the source correction.
tldr: The overlap-population treatment effect is a ratio of expected conditional covariance and variance. The covariate density is unknown and merely bounded, both marginal regressions are H\"older smooth, and the conditional joint-success probability remains unrestricted. The total consecutive-edge release and its covering interval give a density-free benchmark, while exactly normalized paired priors give a finite converse. The smooth, privacy-dominated, and saturated regimes are closed; the remaining rough weak-privacy regime has a proved numerical bracket and polynomial exponents, with unmatched subpolynomial factors. The paired laws also give a nonprivate expected-conditional-covariance obstruction on the containing published DCDR model, without transferring an upper bound. The new content is a total edge benchmark, a finite normalized marked-occupancy converse, and an exact diagnostic rejecting the raw factorial correction; stable sharp attainment, the optimal normalized testing geometry, and the relation between honest length and root mean squared error remain open.
gap: McClean et al. (2025, arXiv v3, Section 2.1) leave minimax expected conditional covariance estimation with a nonsmooth design density unresolved. Their bounded-density Assumption 2 is separate from smoothness requirements. Zeng et al. (2024, Section 5.2) show that unknown category masses enter the same covariance/variance causal ratio. Existing pure-private WATE releases do not determine its minimax accuracy or uniform finite-sample interval length over the present full class.
fill: Derive the explicit point and interval frontiers from a total stable marked correction and legal normalized testing priors. Certify the smooth, privacy-dominated, and saturated reductions, and determine the remaining rough weak-privacy factors and degree transitions without adding nuisance smoothness or a pooling restriction.
